content.comment_body: Hello. I'd like to replicate a block connection from the example program in my own, but I'm not sure how to do it. In the documentation archive, there's timer.lsc (B001 & B010) as an example, and my own program is 220_2_english.lsc (B001 & B010). When I add the B010 block again in my program, a letter appears in the display—but only after a second elapses. I want to address this, following the structure of the example program. How and where can I set up the B010 block reference button like in the example? I've connected B001 and B010 in my own program, but the result isn't matching the example.

Hello [user_name], and welcome to the forum. Your setup in 220_2_english seems correct. The timer B010 uses seconds as its time base, as you desired. The 'm' in the display shows that the format is in mm:ss.

Hello [user_name], thank you for the warm welcome and quick response! I see what you mean—it's functioning properly (showing 00:00m as min:sec). Is it possible for the display to show only seconds? In the example program, B001 and B010 are connected by a contact, is that the same as in my program? There doesn't seem to be a visible connection line between the blocks in the example program.

The example program was made for [version_no] [article_no], while your program is for [version_no] [article_no]. Since [product_name] [article_no], handling of the reference function is different—you connect the parameter output to the parameter input by drawing a line below the blocks. Before [article_no], referenced blocks were set directly in the block properties. How do you configure references between blocks in [product_name] [version_no]?
Thanks for the help and information, [user_name].
Hello [user_name], you're welcome. Has your issue been resolved now?

analysis.insight_summary: Users face difficulty when trying to transfer block connections, especially timer and counter blocks, from example programs to custom setups using different hardware and software versions. The different methods required for configuration across hardware generations add confusion, particularly regarding visual programming and display settings. Version-specific documentation and clear configuration processes are lacking, leading to user uncertainty.
analysis.user_expectations: Users wish for the timer block (B010) to function and display time exactly like the example program, preferably in seconds only, and are looking for clear guidance on handling differences across versions while connecting blocks in [product_name] software.
